b: With the ocean all around, Achyuta lies in his endless sleep. From his navel, the world of Truth is born. First, Brahma is born. At his very birth he understands the purpose of his birth. Through the lotus stalk that rose from the navel-lotus, wisdom reaches him too. He begins the work of creation. All he knows is how to create. Creation spreads. It grows vast. Stars are born. Planets are born. The five elements are born. And a desire is born in him too. To echo the sleep of Keshava on his banyan leaf, he made an island with water all around. On the body of that endless sleeper he feels heat and coolness together. So he made rain and sunshine come together. Just as the navel-lotus rose upwards, he made a land of mountains as high as the sky.. Like the countless thousands of lives born from him, he made the cloud-messengers strike the mountain peaks and set the drops of water flowing in floods on every side. The water poured out greenness and plenty. In that greenness, living things were born. The living things that were born happily gave their land a thousand holy names. As the flow of time carried many of them away, from those that remained those beings happily chose the name Lanka.

When the pure Tamil wind, carrying the scent of Kerala, blows in from the north, the fragrance of Aryan Sinhala spreads in from the south. Here and there the magic of English words is sprinkled in like a spray of rain. A Buddha born somewhere else set up his seat here. Knowing the secrets of creation himself, he let them wander in many people's thoughts. The Buddha's way became Buddhism. Buddhism became the Dharma. On the foundation of that Dharma, Lanka rose and stood tall.

The young maiden called Nature, in an excess of love, swept Lanka into her arms. In the closeness of that embrace, wherever milk flowed from her breasts, it became forests and groves. Closeness brought heat too. Some places, unable to bear the heat of her breath, dried up. Grieved by the drought, she gave them drops of kisses as a gift, and from them sprang a few trees and grasslands. Varuna, who often held this scene before the mirror of his mind, joined with Vayu and danced with joy, thinking of it again and again. As the dance goes on, rain and storm blow.

Hearing the pleading voices of young women wearing jingling anklets, Indra sent down the wish-giving tree. Because it gave many kinds of fruit for so long, it became the palmyra. Kamadhenu, who came with it, multiplied into herds of cattle. It ended others' hunger. Seeing the world of the gods come to earth, the one who burned the three cities became the three-eyed fruit and spread across the whole island. And with him came the snakes of the one who drank poison, and their offspring, leopards and little fish, beetles and birds of the sky: many kinds of life came. Because of a delay of a few seconds, the lion lost its place. Hearing this, man grew worried and thumped his chest, calling himself the lion's heir. In time he built the Lion Rock too.. Not forgetting the Dharma, he set up dagobas; and in the land of one who hated war and followed the Buddha, he built forts and battlements. The daughter of Time grew angry. Leaving the spires of the Dharma standing, she took many of the others into herself

As the wheel of time rolled on, human invention began to spread like a cancer. But countless hearts stand longing to protect what she has left behind. No one knows the day the daughter of Time will grow angry again. But let the righteous anger of nature's guardians protect the Lanka I saw. Let it endure in the world
note: Achyuta and Keshava are names of Vishnu, who sleeps on the cosmic serpent Ananta (and, as a child, floats on a banyan leaf); Brahma is born from the lotus that rises from his navel. Varuna and Vayu are the gods of rain and wind. The wish-giving tree (karpaga tharu) is what Jaffna Tamils call the palmyra palm, and Kamadhenu is the wish-giving cow. The "three-eyed fruit" is the coconut, likened to three-eyed Shiva, who burned the three cities and swallowed poison. Sri Lanka has no lions, though the Sinhala people trace their origin to a lion; the Lion Rock is Sigiriya, and dagobas are Buddhist stupas.
